𝐂𝐫𝐮𝐞𝐥 𝐈𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬, 𝟏𝟗𝟗𝟗.⁣
⁣
When Cruel Intentions arrived in 1999, it felt like the movie every teenager wanted to see but probably wasn’t supposed to. It was provocative, scandalous and completely soaked in the excess of the late ’90s. ⁣
⁣
But the story itself was already centuries old. The film is a modern adaptation of Les Liaisons dangereuses, the 1782 French novel that also inspired Dangerous Liaisons (1988). Instead of aristocrats playing cruel games with each other’s lives, Cruel Intentions moves the story to wealthy Manhattan teenagers. Ryan Phillippe’s Sebastian and Sarah Michelle Gellar’s Kathryn are privileged step-siblings who treat seduction and manipulation almost like a sport. Their latest game revolves around Annette, played by Reese Witherspoon. Sebastian makes a bet that he can seduce her, only to discover that his feelings aren’t as easy to control as he expected. That’s where the movie becomes more than its reputation suggests. Yes, Cruel Intentions has the infamous Sarah Michelle Gellar and Selma Blair kiss, outrageous dialogue and enough manipulation to fill an entire soap opera. But behind the surface is a surprisingly dark story about people discovering that their actions eventually have consequences.⁣
⁣
The casting is a huge reason it works. Gellar creates one of the most memorable villains of the era, Phillippe gives Sebastian just enough vulnerability to make his transformation believable, and Witherspoon provides the sincerity the story needs. Then there’s the soundtrack. Placebo, Counting Crows, Fatboy Slim and, of course, The Verve’s “Bitter Sweet Symphony” accompanying an ending that remains inseparable from the movie itself.⁣
⁣
Cruel Intentions isn’t subtle, and it was never trying to be. It’s a late-’90s time capsule filled with lust, betrayal, privilege and revenge. More than 25 years later, it’s still dangerously easy to watch.⁣
⁣

source_details.synopsis: Cruel Intentions is a 1999 American teen romantic drama film written and directed by Roger Kumble, and starring Ryan Phillippe, Sarah Michelle Gellar, Reese Witherspoon, and Selma Blair. The film, set in New York City among rich high schoolers, is a modern retelling of Pierre Choderlos de Laclos' 1782 novel Les Liaisons dangereuses. Initially a smaller-budget independent film, it was picked up by Columbia Pictures and widely released on March 5, 1999. Despite mixed critical reviews, the performances of Gellar, Phillippe, and Witherspoon were praised and the film grossed $76 million worldwide.
